The good news is that states are fighting back, with 25 states suing the USPS and the Trump administration to stop this blatantly unconstitutional power grab.
The corrupt Supreme Court has allowed Trump’s scheme to proceed, but this rule is creating chaos in our courts with one lower court judge lifting a nationwide injunction this week, while another issued a temporary restraining order against this USPS scheme.
In my district 60% of voters cast their ballots early, with many utilizing mail-in ballots. This is particularly important for working people who can’t get time off from work to vote; for older voters and people with disabilities who may have mobility issues or trouble securing a ride to the polls; for U.S. service members and citizens living abroad; and for students who may go to school out of state.
During the last presidential election, nearly one-third of all voters voted by mail―roughly 48 million voters. **Now just imagine if the U.S. Postal Service was allowed to decide who should and shouldn’t receive their ballot?!**
**Just as the USPS has done for generations, it must deliver lawful ballots and election information without delays, retaliation, or new political conditions.**

Donald Trump wants your
name. Your DOB. Your address. Your driver's license number. And the last
four digits of your SSN. Simply because you're registered to vote.

One of his executive orders demanded every state hand over its entire
voter roll — millions of Americans' private data — to the federal
government.

Thirty states and D.C. said no. So Trump’s DOJ sued them all.

Judges have blocked his power grab 22 times. But that’s not enough for
Trump. His loyalist Attorney General, Todd Blanche, just said taking this
fight to the Supreme Court is "absolutely" a possibility.^1

Before he was Attorney General, Blanche was Trump's personal lawyer — he
defended Trump through 34 felony convictions. Now he runs the DOJ, and
he's the one deciding whether to ask the Supreme Court to override 22
rulings and hand Trump the voter data he couldn't get any other way.

This is about control. Trump is using the DOJ he's turned into a personal
weapon to get his hands on every American's voter data to interfere in the
midterm elections and cement his grip on power before voters can push
back.

We're not sitting on the sidelines. Demand Justice PAC is fighting to
expose this corruption and hold the DOJ accountable. But we can't do it
without you.

By Illinois Review

Lyons Township Clerk Elyse Hoffenberg released surveillance footage Thursday night showing her after-hours kiss with Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek — and the video is now raising new questions about how she previously characterized the encounter.

Hoffenberg, who is married and is the Democratic candidate for Cook County Board District 17, had described the July incident as a “peck” and told Patch that she immediately told Landek the contact was “inappropriate” and that Landek apologized.

But the newly released footage provides a fuller picture of the encounter.

here in New Hampshire.

We’re running out of time to change the direction of this race, so we need

Chris

name: Swing Left
subject: Texas, Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, and Mississippi Senate races are within reach
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Why we expanded our Senate map:
#
Hi there,
We recently expanded Swing Left’s target list of competitive swing districts and states—adding 11 new U.S. House districts and 3 new U.S. Senate races, plus moving 11 House districts, 2 Senate races, and 2 Governor’s races from “Reach” to “Must-Flip” or “Must-Hold.”
**Today, we want to dive deeper into the rationale behind updating our map of U.S. Senate targets.**
Across red states, voters are feeling the direct economic strain of Donald Trump’s tariffs, rising costs, and the ongoing war in Iran. Coupled with an incredibly strong slate of Democratic and independent candidates who are exciting the base while appealing to broad electorates, the Senate map is opening up far beyond traditional battlegrounds.
While nonpartisan ratings shifts—like recent updates from the _Cook Political Report_ on the Texas and Iowa Senate races—reflect this changing environment, those ratings are only one factor in our decisions. We take a data-driven approach to every target, analyzing ground-level polling, grassroots fundraising, volunteer capacity, local organizing infrastructure, and direct campaign operations.
Based on those factors, here’s how we are expanding our Senate target map.
**Upgraded to Must-Flip**
In **Texas** , Democratic State Representative **James Talarico** has built a grassroots-driven campaign that is drawing national attention. Meanwhile, Republican nominee Ken Paxton enters the general election carrying massive political baggage from years of ethics scandals, federal investigations, and a contentious primary fight. Public and private polling now show Talarico leading in this race. This November, Texas voters have the chance to make history and elect a Democratic U.S Senator—something that hasn’t occurred since 1988.
In **Iowa** , Democratic State Representative **Josh Turek** is running a campaign dedicated to delivering for Iowans. His opponent, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson, a Trump supporter, would lock in a far-right vote in the U.S. Senate. Polls are showing Turek running within the margin of error, or roughly ahead or behind three points, making Iowa’s Senate race a more-than-viable path to winning back the chamber.
Both the Texas and Iowa Senate races were recently shifted from Lean Republican to Toss-Up by independent political analysts at _Cook Political Report_.
**New Reach Targets**
We are also expanding into three new **Reach** races. While these races will be tougher to win, targeting them lets us capitalize on growing backlash toward Republicans while building the long-term grassroots infrastructure needed to break Republican strongholds for years to come.
In **Nebraska** , independent **Dan Osborn** is building on his historic 2024 run, where he earned 46.5% of the vote, to challenge Senator Pete Ricketts. With no Democrat in the race, Osborn represents our best opportunity to defeat an incumbent Republican in a state hard-hit by agricultural tariffs.
In **Kansas** , Rev. **Adam Hamilton** , founding pastor of the nation’s largest United Methodist church, outraised Republican incumbent Roger Marshall 6-to-1 last quarter. His unique ability to connect across party lines makes Kansas a genuine sleeper race against Marshall’s unpopular record.
In **Mississippi** , District Attorney **Scott Colom** has a proven track record of winning across party lines. By mobilizing Black voters who make up one-third of the electorate and tapping into widespread anger over living costs and tariffs, Colom provides a clear path to victory against Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Taking back the Senate majority is within our reach this November. But even if Democrats fall short of a Senate majority, every race we win in 2026 matters enormously.
Every seat gained weakens Republicans’ grip on power and strengthens the ability to push back on the MAGA agenda. And because Senate seats won in 2026 won’t be up again until 2032, they also matter for our long-term strategy.
Winning Senate seats now lays the groundwork for a governing majority if Democrats win back the White House in 2028. A Democratic president taking office in 2029 will need a Senate ready to confirm nominees, pass legislation, and govern effectively from day one.
[**One of the best ways to make an impact on these races is by making a donation to Swing Left’s Win the Senate Fund to directly support Democrats in our Must-Flip House races and our Must-Win Senate races.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260830-2620&t=1&akid=2620%2E1562180%2Ealo0W7)
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-balance-of-power-2026.KwVigu&refcode=em20260830-2620&t=2&akid=2620%2E1562180%2Ealo0W7)**
Thank you for being a part of this effort to flip the Senate this fall.
— The Swing Left Team
P.S [**If you’d like to see the full list of target races, you can find it here!**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1219?utm_source=em20260830-2620&t=3&akid=2620%2E1562180%2Ealo0W7)

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260830-1&t=4&refcode2=2620_1562180_alo0W7&akid=2620%2E1562180%2Ealo0W7)

I firmly believe that, and I think we're at a point, certainly in Alaska, where we need to rise up and say we expect a Congress that helps all of us and isn't just in it for the millionaires and billionaires.
Peter, it’s Mary Peltola here with a humble request: **[Can you please split a $10 contribution between Heartland Patriots and my campaign as we begin the general election?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107977?refcode=em20260830-10854&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=1&akid=10854%2E614464%2EVIHjNi)**
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107977?refcode=em20260830-10854&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10854%2E614464%2EVIHjNi)**
I’m sorry to be so upfront because – to be honest – Yup’ik people don’t like asking for money. In fact, I hate it! **But I wouldn’t ask if your support wasn’t so important.**
Yup’ik people also believe that when we set our mind to something, we can do anything. We use the word "ikayuquluta" when we work together to overcome challenges.
I firmly believe that, and I think we're at a point, certainly in Alaska, where we need to rise up and say we expect a Congress that helps all of us and isn't just in it for the millionaires and billionaires.
That means we all have to do our part.
This team has stood by my side since I launched this campaign just a few months ago, and I’m hopeful that today will be no different.
So I have to humbly ask:
**[Can you split a contribution of $10, or whatever you can afford, between Heartland Patriots and my campaign to help us win on November 3? With everyone chipping in just a little bit, I know we can get where we need to be.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/107977?refcode=em20260830-10854&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=3&akid=10854%2E614464%2EVIHjNi)**

| [|

| | | | Peter, The Trump administration officially advanced a plan to shred the 25-year-old Roadless Rule. With a single stroke, they are stripping protections from 45 million acres of pristine national forests, opening them to road construction and commercial logging. [**We’re calling on all those who love and want to protect our public lands to join us in fighting back by rushing an emergency $3 donation this morning >>>.**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/ta4M1qN8wssZQERGgSjBkg~~/AAUS1hA~/5qXPSnols_nE-t8d8HdVeVLdTrXzKGpYI8LAfWrS4GYM-PIF2G3eLtfmuRdG6ccdQvLxYASb4lQZsaijaehTfgVo0kTzlu3SbYDCLYKz08FGOKRlpQz28pwzi0WS4iLqCsSEYlDHUiS7LrLsSDxIJYA_RtytTvP3mFP1PqzPRZ2zdFaQsU_DDjR2B3NE23zZ12wSRResulEtNIBHMoQ7jl29UkkkD2uJiqO-nuLm619h8_CQUDr98qFZl69Q82X3) We are talking about nearly 30% of all national forest land in America—including 9 million acres in Alaska's Tongass National Forest—wiped out and handed directly to the timber lobby. Politicians cheering this corporate selloff, like Montana Governor Greg Gianforte, want you to believe this is an "emergency" measure to reduce wildfire risk. They are actually trying to convince you that the best way to save an untouched, old-growth forest is to clear-cut it and pave a road right through the middle. **It is a bald-faced lie.** Research shows that 85% of all wildfires are started by human activity. When you bulldoze a road into the deep backcountry, you aren't preventing fires—you are guaranteeing them by inviting in discarded cigarettes, sparks from heavy logging equipment, and highly flammable invasive grasses. Fire ecologists will tell you that fires in remote, roadless areas are actually smaller and less destructive. They don't want to stop forest fires. They want to boost commercial logging by 25%, **and they need your public lands to do it.** [**This is a five-alarm fire for our wild spaces. clean_body: 45 Million Acres at Stake | | | | | Peter, The Trump administration officially advanced a plan to shred the 25-year-old Roadless Rule. With a single stroke, they are stripping protections from 45 million acres of pristine national forests, opening them to road construction and commercial logging. We are talking about nearly 30% of all national forest land in America—including 9 million acres in Alaska's Tongass National Forest—wiped out and handed directly to the timber lobby. Politicians cheering this corporate selloff, like Montana Governor Greg Gianforte, want you to believe this is an "emergency" measure to reduce wildfire risk. They are actually trying to convince you that the best way to save an untouched, old-growth forest is to clear-cut it and pave a road right through the middle. It is a bald-faced lie. Research shows that 85% of all wildfires are started by human activity. When you bulldoze a road into the deep backcountry, you aren't preventing fires—you are guaranteeing them by inviting in discarded cigarettes, sparks from heavy logging equipment, and highly flammable invasive grasses. Fire ecologists will tell you that fires in remote, roadless areas are actually smaller and less destructive. They don't want to stop forest fires. They want to boost commercial logging by 25%, and they need your public lands to do it. You take our land—we take your seat. In light of the Cuyahoga County Democratic Party boycotting Judge4Yourself, I thought it was worth revisiting something I wrote back in November. So little is known about the judges running for office these days, which makes independent vetting and public scrutiny even more important.
# [Stop Treating Judicial Elections Like a Popularity Contest](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3159258&post_id=179843746&utm_source=cross-post&utm_campaign=3159258&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTc5ODQzNzQ2LCJpYXQiOjE3ODgxMDQ5OTUsImV4cCI6MTc5MDY5Njk5NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMxNTkyNTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.AidpNkPraiPqr49K9xx0ietHYFQkNcaCFQDf-qQ7JcM)
### How Cuyahoga County's judge races became uncontested and why that must change.

This one is short, but it is important. It is about electing judges. Every election cycle, voters in Northeast Ohio see a long list of judicial seats on the ballot. Municipal courts. Common Pleas. Appeals courts. Probate. Juvenile. The Ohio Supreme Court.
These positions impact every part of our lives, from traffic violations to wrongful death lawsuits, from custody battles to felony trials that determine whether someone spends life behind bars.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d42e0cb1-a945-48ec-b6a6-39d0f3f0ed81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And out of every elected position in this state, judges receive the least scrutiny. They get the biggest paychecks and the most autonomy, yet we vet them the least.
A Common Pleas judge in Ohio makes around $180k a year. That is more than $1.2M over a six year term. Taxpayer money. Guaranteed. For a job where one individual controls the docket, the schedule, the tone of the courtroom, and the outcomes that shape lives.
In Cleveland and throughout Cuyahoga County, you can see this play out every cycle. Judges campaign like traditional politicians. They shake hands. They appear at ward club meetings. They smile in photos with whoever will stand next to them. They sell their LinkedIn bullet points to the public. They get endorsements from party insiders who often cannot point to a single decision that judge has actually made on the bench.
The problem is not one judge. It is the process.
* * *
**Judges Have Massive Power. We Treat It Like a Popularity Contest**
For almost every other office, there are checks and balances. A city council member is one voice among several. A mayor cannot pass anything without cooperation. A state legislator must work within a chamber. Even the governor has limits.
But in a courtroom, it is one judge who sets the rules. One judge who determines credibility. One judge who controls the clock. One judge who can delay hearings for months or push cases through at light speed. One judge whose interpretation of the law can change the trajectory of a family, a business, a life.
Yet when these candidates come to political club meetings in Northeast Ohio, they rarely get asked real questions. No one presses them on how they manage their docket. No one asks about their courtroom efficiency. No one digs into their past decisions, even when those decisions shaped outcomes for hundreds of families.
Instead, far too often, judges are elected based on good vibes. They seem friendly. They had a nice conversation. They showed up to breakfast at the union hall. They took a selfie with a popular senator. And for that alone, voters hand over one of the most powerful positions in our democracy.
We would never hire anyone else for a $1.2M 6 year contracted job this way.
* * *
**I Am Guilty of This Too**
I am not pointing fingers without pointing one at myself. There have been times when I supported a judge because I liked them. Because they showed up. Because they were personable. Because they had the right letter next to their name.
That is not good enough. Not for a job where one person's decision can determine whether a kid gets a second chance or enters the prison system. Not for a job that decides whether working families win their civil cases or get crushed by a corporation with deep pockets. Not for a job that shapes public safety, fairness, and trust in our entire legal system.
We owe the public better than that.
* * *
**Northeast Ohio 's Real Problem: No Competition**
In Cuyahoga County, the lack of competition is staggering. Many judicial races have only one candidate. In a county that votes heavily Democratic, the primary becomes the real election. And far too often, the primary has been cleared before it even starts. It is a waiting-your-turn culture. A handshake-and-a-nod culture. A "this is our person" culture. And if it doesn't happen that way... then the candidate **cries** (literally I have seen it).
That is not democracy.
Robust primaries force ideas. They force answers. They force candidates to explain how they operate their courtroom, how they treat defendants, how they manage their caseload, and how they interpret the law. When you clear the field, you rob the public of the chance to ask the hard questions.
And judges should face the hardest questions of all.
* * *
**It Is Time To Do Better**
I am going to do better. I am going to dig deeper. I am going to ask harder questions. I am going to treat judicial elections with the seriousness they deserve, and I hope you do too.
A judge is not just another politician. They are the final decision maker on some of the most important moments of our lives. We cannot keep electing them based on name recognition and social media selfies.
We need scrutiny. We need competition. We need accountability. We need real vetting.
And if we want justice in Northeast Ohio to actually work, then we need to start treating these elections like they matter.
Because they do.
## Stay Angry.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: USS Donald J. Trump
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Trump wants Doris Miller’s name stripped from a carrier so he can replace it with his own
#

Peter, Trump’s obsessed with naming things — and naming them after himself, in particular.
~~Gulf of Mexico~~
Gulf of America
~~Lake Ontario~~
Lake America
~~John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts~~
Donald J. Trump and the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts
~~United States Institute of Peace~~
Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace
~~Palm Beach International Airport~~
President Donald J. Trump International Airport
All of this stuff is ridiculous and embarrassing. Makes us look like North Korea. But he’s trying to do something especially egregious right now.
A new fleet of aircraft carriers is being developed, the Ford-class. One of them is named the USS Doris Miller, after a fallen Black sailor from WWII. He was barred from combat jobs because of the color of his skin, but at Pearl Harbor he manned an anti-aircraft gun and shot down two hostile aircraft. He won the Navy Cross, and was killed when his ship was sunk later in the war.
Doris Miller deserves that recognition because he is an American hero. But Trump wants Miller’s name stripped from the carrier so he can replace it with his own. All this after Trump dodged the draft, and while the Navy fights a war Trump started.
~~USS Doris Miller~~
USS Donald J. Trump
This kind of thing — along with a million other things Trump’s done — should shock the conscience of every American. I imagine you already know a lot of this stuff, but the truth is that most people don’t.
We need to retake the House and Senate this November to put a stop to this, but we’ve got a lot of work to do between now and then. I’m going to be out doing that work because I think it’s the most important thing any of us can do right now.
I need your help on this.

# **NYC tenant complaints surge at Mamdani 's command, landlords cry foul**
Tenant complaints in NYC **[have jumped 25% this year](https://substack.com/redirect/140cceba-f889-4092-ab1b-c13e3f70bb04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to over 573,000, with the sharpest increases in Brooklyn (32%) and Queens (29%), following Mayor Zohran Mamdani's efforts encouraging renters to report even minor issues, according to a Post analysis.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/140cceba-f889-4092-ab1b-c13e3f70bb04?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Landlords say the system is being weaponized,** citing frivolous complaints and tenants withholding rent while filing grievances before even contacting building owners; officials, including tenant advocate Cea Weaver, have promoted expanded HPD staffing and enforcement as part of Mamdani's $2 billion "block by block" housing plan.
* **Critics argue the surge reflects a broader push to shift property away from landlords,** while the mayor's office frames it as protecting tenants -- including fast-tracking court processes for unresolved violations. Some property owners say complaints have doubled or more since Mamdani took office, calling the trend unprecedented in decades of ownership.

Republicans are ramping up their attacks against me - personal insults, character smears, baseless TV ads, you name it - and dark-money super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million into this race so far to defeat me.
They're spending so much in North Carolina because they know this race could decide U.S. Senate control. However, that's not the only reason why.
They know that if I'm elected to the U.S. Senate, I won't blindly do President Trump's bidding.
Instead, I'll hold this administration accountable when it hurts people, put working families first and do everything I possibly can to make life better for folks in North Carolina and across the country.
I'm a threat to the GOP's hold on power, but the only way I can fight back against their attacks is by reaching every fundraising goal from here on out. This race will come down to resources, and donations even just a couple bucks matter more than you know.

Republicans are ramping up their attacks against me - personal insults, character smears, baseless TV ads, you name it - and dark-money super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million into this race so far to defeat me. They're spending so much in North Carolina because they know this race could decide U.S. Senate control. However, that's not the only reason why. They know that if I'm elected to the U.S. Senate, I won't blindly do President Trump's bidding. Instead, I'll hold this administration accountable when it hurts people, put working families first and do everything I possibly can to make life better for folks in North Carolina and across the country. I'm a threat to the GOP's hold on power, but the only way I can fight back against their attacks is by reaching every fundraising goal from here on out. This race will come down to resources, and donations even just a couple bucks matter more than you know. Before tomorrow 's end-of-month deadline, I need you with me. I can't hit this goal without you. Thanks for pitching in. Roy Cooper | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Roy Cooper PO Box 1190, Raleigh, NC 27602 ? ?

name: David Hogg
subject: Leadership, the future of the Democratic Party, and what comes next.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Here’s what I’ve been up to.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260830-1&t=1&akid=3946%2E587540%2EwkXWuH)
Peter,
I've been having a series of candid conversations about the state of the Democratic Party and where we go from here. These aren't conversations I take lightly — but they're conversations that are long overdue.
I've been direct about the challenges we face. I've expressed concern that our party has become too comfortable offering voters incremental change when what they're demanding is transformation.
Too often, we package the same old ideas in new wrapping and expect voters to be excited about it. They're not. They're tired of being told to fall in line. They want leaders who will actually fight for them and _produce results._
**On CNN, I suggested that we need _new_ leadership at the DNC because our current approach simply isn't working.** We _keep_ losing races we should be winning. We _keep_ alienating voters who should be part of our coalition. And we _keep_ doubling down on the same strategies while expecting different results.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260830_1_recap.C8OHWS&refcode=em20260830-3946&t=2&akid=3946%2E587540%2EwkXWuH)
I've been critical of a party that has become too focused on positioning itself in the center rather than offering a bold vision for the future. I believe voters are hungry for a clear plan — not just a vote against the other side.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260830_1_recap.C8OHWS&refcode=em20260830-3946&t=3&akid=3946%2E587540%2EwkXWuH)
**They want to know what we stand for, not just what we're against. And when we refuse to offer that vision, we cede the narrative to those who will.**
These comments have not been universally welcomed. But my focus remains on the work ahead.
I'm not interested in engaging in personal feuds or political theater. I'm interested in building something that lasts.
**That work is Leaders We Deserve.**
We are recruiting, training, and funding a new generation of progressive leaders across the country. Young people who are running to fix the issues that matter most to Americans — affordable housing, healthcare, reproductive rights, climate action, and gun violence prevention.
Whether the establishment is ready for them or not, these are the leaders who will shape the future of this party.
We're not waiting for permission from party bosses. We're not asking for a seat at the table. We're building our own table. And we're doing it by investing in candidates who reflect the communities they seek to represent — candidates who understand what working families are going through because they're living it themselves.
We've already seen **significant** success. This cycle alone, we've helped elect 34 candidates, including numerous state legislators, members of Congress, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani. We're building a bench of young leaders who will be the future of this party — and we're proving that this model works.
But we can't sustain this momentum without resources. Identifying promising candidates, training them, funding voter outreach, and supporting them through Election Day requires infrastructure. And that infrastructure doesn't build itself. It takes investment from people who believe in the future we're building.
**[So, Peter, will you make a contribution today to help Leaders We Deserve continue our work? We could use your support before the August deadline.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260830_1_recap.C8OHWS&refcode=em20260830-3946&amount=5&t=4&akid=3946%2E587540%2EwkXWuH)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260830_1_recap.C8OHWS&amount=5&refcode=em20260830-3946&t=23&akid=3946%2E587540%2EwkXWuH)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

| | Peter, This week, I was supposed to be hiking part of the Pacific Crest Trail, starting at Timberline, on Mt. Hood.
We planned the trip to spend time on our public lands and talk about what it will take to protect them for the next generation. But we had to cancel because wildfire smoke made it unsafe to go.
That is clearly a small thing compared to families who have lost homes, communities threatened by fire, or the firefighters putting themselves in harm’s way.
But it also says something about what the wildfire season has become in Oregon. **The places we love are still here. But more and more, there are days when we can't safely enjoy them.**
The hike you planned all year. The camping trip with your kids. The weekend at the lake. The view of the mountains that disappears behind a wall of smoke.
Oregonians have some of the most extraordinary public lands in the country right outside our doors. We hike them. We fish them. We camp in them. We take our kids there and build memories that fill our hearts.
**We shouldn't accept a future where wildfires and smoke increasingly take those experiences away from us.**
And as a lung and critical care doctor, I know the consequences go well beyond a canceled hike. Wildfire smoke sends kids with asthma to the hospital, worsens heart and lung disease, and can make simply stepping outside dangerous for our most vulnerable neighbors.
That's why I introduced the **Climate Health Emergency Act** , and why I'm fighting for serious federal action that treats the climate crisis with the urgency it demands.
Protecting our climate isn't an abstract debate. **It's about protecting our health, our communities, and a way of life that is uniquely Oregon.**
[**Our August fundraising deadline is tomorrow. Can we count on your support to keep up the fight for our public lands and our communities?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138192432/643367388/320772526?refcode=x_260830_PNWfires_act&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMDk5MDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZDk1OTI0OGItOGNhNC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=oTmPqWV7NUxvPvi1W3Cwsl35e4-fzPuv4dxiYoeO86I=)

clean_body: | | | = | | Peter, This week, I was supposed to be hiking part of the Pacific Crest Trail, starting at Timberline, on Mt. Hood. We planned the trip to spend time on our public lands and talk about what it will take to protect them for the next generation. But we had to cancel because wildfire smoke made it unsafe to go. That is clearly a small thing compared to families who have lost homes, communities threatened by fire, or the firefighters putting themselves in harm’s way. But it also says something about what the wildfire season has become in Oregon. The places we love are still here. But more and more, there are days when we can't safely enjoy them. The hike you planned all year. The camping trip with your kids. The weekend at the lake. The view of the mountains that disappears behind a wall of smoke. Oregonians have some of the most extraordinary public lands in the country right outside our doors. We hike them. We fish them. We camp in them. We take our kids there and build memories that fill our hearts. We shouldn't accept a future where wildfires and smoke increasingly take those experiences away from us. And as a lung and critical care doctor, I know the consequences go well beyond a canceled hike. Wildfire smoke sends kids with asthma to the hospital, worsens heart and lung disease, and can make simply stepping outside dangerous for our most vulnerable neighbors. That's why I introduced the Climate Health Emergency Act , and why I'm fighting for serious federal action that treats the climate crisis with the urgency it demands. Protecting our climate isn't an abstract debate. I wanted to give you a personal update of what I’ve been up to, as you’ve always been a supporter I can count on:
**I got back from a congressional trip to Ukraine** and sat down with NPR to talk about what I saw — a country five years into this war, rationing air defense missiles while Russian ballistic strikes hit their cities harder every week. I told them plainly: we have to cut through the bureaucratic excuses and get Ukraine the weapons they need. There is no other option.
**Two days later, I was on Morning Joe** making the same case — and then that night on CNN, talking about North Korea funneling aid to Russia and Trump handing out pardons like party favors.
**In between all of that, Senator Durbin and I sent a letter demanding answers** on immigrants missing "mega court" hearings that are being scheduled with almost no notice — hearings that can end in deportation before someone even knows they're supposed to show up.
**By Saturday, I was on MSNOW** talking about Trump's newest tariff threats and serious security concerns swirling around Natalie Harp. By Monday morning, back on CNN discussing his latest tariffs on Canada and new sanctions on Iran. And by Monday afternoon, I was announcing a $1 million community project funding award for the DuPage Water Commission to create a water system that filters out contaminants like lead and microplastics.
I'm telling you all this for one reason: I am not slowing down. If anything, I'm working harder — because there is too much at stake to coast.

Peter, It’s hard to believe, but we’re wrapping up August and soon enough, November will be here. It’s going to be an incredibly challenging few months before Election Day and I know that we’ll face them together. But first, let me just say thank you for being a part of this incredible journey. When we launched this reelection campaign, I never could have imagined how much grassroots strength we’d build. Through all the challenges we’ve faced, together we’ve created a movement that puts our community first over Republican chaos. **And because of you, I’m more optimistic than ever about not just our chance to take back the House on November 3rd, but the future of our country.** We now have just about two months left to make the final case to voters across the country that Democrats are offering real solutions to the challenges families and communities are facing while Republicans are offering more chaos. Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

body:

| Friend,
---
In May, I was taken to the hospital, fell into a coma, placed on a ventilator, and read my last rites.
---
And yet, _here I still am_. In so many ways, it’s miraculous.
---
But ever since my brush with death, I’ve been thinking a lot about my life’s work, my legacy...
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
__
---
I fought the Mafia, I fought violent criminals, I fought corruption, and I fought the Deep State agents who tried to frame and destroy my client and friend – President Trump.
---
But today, as an 82-year-old man, I see that my greatest fight _still_ lies ahead.
---
**Perhaps I was saved for a very specific reason – to ensure the Radical Left can never again do to anyone else what they’ve done to President Trump and me.**
---
_And now, I have the chance to WIN that battle._
---
**You see, a vengeful Democrat Attorney General is making me stand in yet another RIGGED trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even President Trump can save me with a _federal_ pardon in _state_ court.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
__
---
And my “crime?” Refusing to denounce the TRUTH.
---
This trial really is the Left’s last-ditch effort to try and get me to finally throw in the towel.
---
But they simply don’t understand. They can strip me of all I’m worth – _all I’ll ever be worth_ – but what I _REFUSE_ to surrender to the Democrats and their Deep State thugs is my LEGACY!
---
**I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.”**
---
__"For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?"_ (Mark 8:36)_
---
This FINAL BATTLE for my freedom is about ensuring this injustice will _NEVER_ _AGAIN_ happen to another innocent patriot all for standing by what he knows to be right and true.
---
I pray that in the end when we’ve won this trial, _that_ will be my legacy.
---
But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: _honest and compassionate patriots like _YOU_._
---
Friend, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it!
---
**_But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense humanly possible to defeat this radical Democrat Attorney General who is hell-bent on locking me up for the rest of my life._**
---
[**Please make a contribution to the Rudy Defense Trust to ensure I have the resources needed to retain a top-notch defense team in what is now the FINAL BATTLE for my freedom and justice.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | We recently uncovered something happening in a remote patch What we found? I’ll never forget stepping out of the D.C. jail that chilly morning in 2019. I’d just been released after protesting on the steps of the Capitol for climate action. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138193969/643373085/2105508926?refcode=ea.93457ce1-90a4-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ms=ea.93457ce1-90a4-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjkzNDU3Y2UxLTkwYTQtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWE4ZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=yjeRzeynmgloL45o09a9kbaCwlmiqIdXUi-SDdv4GGw=) _**[Source](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138193970/643373086/1389313699?refcode=ea.93457ce1-90a4-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ms=ea.93457ce1-90a4-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjkzNDU3Y2UxLTkwYTQtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOWE4ZCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=yjeRzeynmgloL45o09a9kbaCwlmiqIdXUi-SDdv4GGw=&emci=77e66b6f-f2a2-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&emdi=93457ce1-90a4-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ceid=4823105)**_ As I started to leave, a Fox TV reporter rushed over and stuck a mic in my face while his camera rolled. "Why have you done this, gone to jail?" he asked with an edge in his voice. "To get you to cover climate," I replied. **That exchange captures exactly why I've put my body on the line over and over again — to force people to pay attention to the crisis that's staring us all in the face.** But I knew that raising awareness wouldn’t be enough. The more I learned about the climate crisis, the more I realized that building power was essential to changing the way this country does business. Protesting got people’s attention. It forced conversations. But nothing is going to change at the scale we need if we don't change the people in power. **That's why I started JanePAC. My goal was and is to move people from concern to action, and it's why I'm grateful to you, friend. This community is proof that we’re not in this fight alone.** Together, we’re backing candidates who aren’t afraid to take on corporate polluters. Leaders who understand that science demands urgency. Morality demands courage. And the moment demands boldness. As Trump and his MAGA allies auction off our planet to the highest bidder, we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines anymore. We need to keep pushing for leaders in office who understand that the window to prevent climate catastrophe is closing fast. **[I'm not slowing down. And I hope you won't either. We've set a goal to raise $30,000 by tomorrow at midnight to power our critical work ahead, and we're counting on supporters like you to help us get there. Will you join me in this fight by chipping in whatever you can? clean_body: The answer is simple. | I’ll never forget stepping out of the D.C. jail that chilly morning in 2019. I’d just been released after protesting on the steps of the Capitol for climate action. = As I started to leave, a Fox TV reporter rushed over and stuck a mic in my face while his camera rolled. "Why have you done this, gone to jail?" he asked with an edge in his voice. "To get you to cover climate," I replied. That exchange captures exactly why I've put my body on the line over and over again — to force people to pay attention to the crisis that's staring us all in the face. But I knew that raising awareness wouldn’t be enough. The more I learned about the climate crisis, the more I realized that building power was essential to changing the way this country does business. Protesting got people’s attention. It forced conversations. But nothing is going to change at the scale we need if we don't change the people in power. That's why I started JanePAC. My goal was and is to move people from concern to action, and it's why I'm grateful to you, friend. This community is proof that we’re not in this fight alone. Together, we’re backing candidates who aren’t afraid to take on corporate polluters. Leaders who understand that science demands urgency. Morality demands courage. And the moment demands boldness. As Trump and his MAGA allies auction off our planet to the highest bidder, we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines anymore. By Illinois Review

While Lyons Township Clerk Elyse Hoffenberg faces mounting scrutiny over an after-hours kiss captured on government surveillance video, the other person on the tape has largely escaped the spotlight.

Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek — a former Democratic state senator, longtime Lyons Township Democratic committeeman and current appointee of Gov. JB Pritzker — has remained publicly silent.

So has Pritzker.

Landek is not simply a local Democratic political figure. He currently serves on the Illinois Finance Authority, a state board whose members are appointed by the governor. State records show Landek has served on the authority since August 2023 and currently holds a term extending through July 2028.

Peter,

It's me, Tommy Tuberville.

Throughout my life, I've been called many names. Whether it's Coach, Dad, Husband, or Senator, I've always led by example for those who depend on me. By the end of the year, I'm hoping you'll be able to call me Governor, too.

**This email is a little longer, but it's worth your time.** [**I’m humbly asking you to read it through and consider donating to my campaign for Alabama’s next Governor when you’re finished.**](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=7bc20a70db6845fcb19e4ca37c603c9a&_e=3G-ZkbjiGINtvF9ZqneEyZFd-6_DrpSLHXUuRokO2AnX1XIJXio6rYYjd7LZ1htoeNjy8PaxFH1rhJF5B7j0shjK4zyGqzWM2sP7_rWgaLl7r4cwz9AcF-lze8oSaqVV-pzkT6gM2gBGgbMt-U-4WCQerFYKFfydI3eBlvsL6M8TE_DVaoVXV6rVmJbyftpyb015-S00C8mQAYHj9_aCaEFZGUMo7mVyPsOAonhjg8IwwJmtT5UzKPQNlqV2C-0NFN0OE0KgWOsQg7ODaYgEBMx01zvV1qUQ44DsZqpjWLpRSF5vzcocZABRr2V24VWUk_gE-auknFjoVwDNUjypKtyu1fyCO2FA-pLpwiSNO0uYINfW2LslVpsnzCggrJcB03_czydnDfZVoDK_8TQRhuXBkWHVWOMvPbF4g5YPDxOPXrpWTovJXNuGGR3teU94ftnirKQXuKWGHzuPWThjo-uhITm4QfoXBDpAbAO016nnku6NMp8KZmzAlGZfeAqclXk464pvwuKRz8TdSXVGi2WC8-f37AeicgtmExF8qMlIyxdcPUfQiZ-gDzG1yD0m)

[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=7bc20a70db6845fcb19e4ca37c603c9a&_e=3G-ZkbjiGINtvF9ZqneEyZFd-6_DrpSLHXUuRokO2AnX1XIJXio6rYYjd7LZ1htoeNjy8PaxFH1rhJF5B7j0shjK4zyGqzWM2sP7_rWgaLl7r4cwz9AcF-lze8oSaqVV-pzkT6gM2gBGgbMt-U-4WCQerFYKFfydI3eBlvsL6M8TE_DVaoVXV6rVmJbyftpyyvAixGJf6UJ_9t-tz9yalyP-27TfLUIABhuTDwRr86Yq2Tr-S9C1yjmnfKVysSN9B0PIAt5RV2So6AAurOI7NTr_ZjRt-_KchwrmekOMkua35Vf6v-QjgDmh1pPoqU8nqAsWxLUN6Qrfm9jgIAoEdGdY18eCHSQ2Oun9Iu-vczvhAfppmZB8ARAYwMoHrdEQrkmf9t4r_thkFNOvko2_udFXzccWsW-Ea_aW3A0Q3USP7kl3eQuq70Y1PLuq2snhJGzphvXw4uMuOSRr1HSShjASSJTGW9kIbjTp6gEM-aMBBZp8A4omjHw5AYOUqU94fGT9aQoVcveAsVX5jcdpSrz-hkwpBS0ihqaxWschUaTIrFSaeqNH6DVhe0ZBYoGY)
I was born in Camden, Arkansas, as the third of three children to my parents, Olive and Charles Tuberville. They raised me to consistently work hard and stand on principle, which I've brought with me every step of my life.

I met my wife, Suzanne, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans in 1989. We married three years later and have two amazing children, Tucker and Troy. _**They continue to make me proud every single day.**_

[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=7bc20a70db6845fcb19e4ca37c603c9a&_e=3G-ZkbjiGINtvF9ZqneEyZFd-6_DrpSLHXUuRokO2AnX1XIJXio6rYYjd7LZ1htoeNjy8PaxFH1rhJF5B7j0shjK4zyGqzWM2sP7_rWgaLl7r4cwz9AcF-lze8oSaqVV-pzkT6gM2gBGgbMt-U-4WCQerFYKFfydI3eBlvsL6M8TE_DVaoVXV6rVmJbyftpyLT3Q9zJFKWyG5gDXVhgYlmvq4rkjy99UWRAhAvyMa57W5pLx16nD5x5FaX5Jpu-rpfmR7wSGGzei6Cj0n3OgXx6z9WBcZxg4MoBdI_FhNw6EHxW0__FLmL5oXQg84nCUKAcSb_gVL2xw6xNNI2Mkv4YpUoCXzRnykpR43pixsKg5HLkxPsKyr1D7Zdav5QnJR8nBITjrVa452CFtYbKZtLPHD9I16gjNobnxxZq-bjEBJHLP0Q6btwB3_DFXXr1oXLfyaoiv2c1bdKg_rd94u-PLDFmxXT-3mVMHLX1-gJrOPuupiOXcCFd_azqaOj2XHM91glSWVBttkvYcM1u-6mKSyaI_bub0yFpJd67yJ0YkFJ6k4o9KJy8l1KhONx0e)
After graduating from SAU, I took my first coaching job at Hermitage High School before graduating to the college level as an assistant coach at Arkansas State University.

Just two years later, I started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, where I went on to become their defensive coordinator. By the time I left the U, we had created one of the most storied programs in college football history. We won three AP national championships, and I coached future Hall-of-Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

[](http://links.tubervilleforalabama.com/u/click?_t=b8b4efbe79f64b579dfa7d8da685a7a9&_m=7bc20a70db6845fcb19e4ca37c603c9a&_e=3G-ZkbjiGINtvF9ZqneEyZFd-6_DrpSLHXUuRokO2AnX1XIJXio6rYYjd7LZ1htoeNjy8PaxFH1rhJF5B7j0shjK4zyGqzWM2sP7_rWgaLl7r4cwz9AcF-lze8oSaqVV-pzkT6gM2gBGgbMt-U-4WCQerFYKFfydI3eBlvsL6M8TE_DVaoVXV6rVmJbyftpySvE_euj8-89bBWi46U3QrTzjEum-aVYuVwetsC7vMgxK-Z55K74fqgCdhEKra4BFiqNNRPwiKzn7c01ibv3pObR97P3po530KdRM_xudWu6DQxaxNvh8rzY-iHB-GNvw4rBPuN1bN1o_8E_wvq1-h3uXBdAoFPQZHnH5k3ru5PuXqcfTCVY93GqYHqX3lo9yuUhtxnh1oTDKc42BhTUb7jbQUjkjmdG7FNI8fKmBmTkp5J2alqGIe4-ki6EJyld4LcOIK4cMxH4M3r2aZ782-w4rlm5tZcKj_6HqlNAcXlvuO6d2Wg_67JbpCBQ9lsxcBmQD1TnJlLhZgebjc7y4IHIF0inzF5wy-doBO4SgW8Q13yH7IeyNPQfdZ_b5h4_N)
I spent a short stint as the head coach for Ole Miss before becoming the head coach for the Auburn Tigers in 1998. I solidified my career there, making eight consecutive bowl appearances, winning five SEC Western Division Titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004 when I was named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year, among other awards.

I continued coaching at Texas Tech University and the University of Cincinnati until I retired from coaching in 2016 as one of the top 50 most-winning college football coaches of all time. But I wasn't done winning just yet.

**In 2020, I went from Coach Tuberville to Senator Tuberville. After talking to my fellow Alabamians, I was enlightened by President Trump's concerns about the direction of our country, and I decided to do something about it. I ran for the United States Senate and won.**

Sixty-five days.

If you know me, you know I’m not someone who sits around waiting for things to happen. I roll up my sleeves and get to work.

We have just 65 days until Election Day, and on November 4th, I want to look back at these next few weeks knowing that we did everything I could to take back the House.

Will you join me? Chip in even just $6.50 today to support our work to elect Democrats in toss-up districts so we’ll have every gavel, every subpoena, and every oversight tool required to hold this Administration accountable. President Trump and his allies in Congress think they can roll over our communities, strip away reproductive freedom, gut VA benefits for our veterans, and purge nonpartisan, hard-working civil servants.

| | Dear Friend,

In the spring of 1775, a handful of farmers and tradesmen stood their ground against the greatest military power on earth.

They didn't know how the story would end.

But they knew that freedom was worth fighting for.

The "shot heard 'round the world" set in motion a chain of events that led to the greatest experiment in self-government the world has ever known.

That's why I'm excited to share something special with you.

**The White House recently asked Hillsdale College to assist the Salute to America 250 Task Force in producing a new free video series, [_The Story of America_](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/LA9DP4ZOYsjn1wtPTTch34VI3MRolUegF-KGB75NeZom61EHQ1cYj-ypaVgCp3fA_KvgF9QWa2Oz_MaWEC4UyCbmICVBDTlhrxKt3QGKdzKTMLBCzyG7AsOXshxBLxWnFX0bJfZ4xqlNvFjahESDO_7YcuGSaalZB6iUo47_K66nows4pXkT0mIGRs5SBTPbP-fT2yjcUJ0RKDZ1ZMYoB2cnP6U0H9CjpNv_mTp8P6963tOHEtnQ09cyScwUkslt_yfYTf_ROpzJDpTUidOUUIy3a1aIDliHrtLLtoDQ3m1sjhs7ouE0L8n764ENOZmegLtJydlRxRO9Q5KC-LNbYNvEYvTLZrhlTSbY2qCpa--R2riCynufRdWbk3Y5WPoRJxjyvWRQc4I5rccUAMb68_vgoxVMqi_aheYKtrgY3zvyoAF7Crg9fiurapWTnOtEyk3YzEKBiJDUXdPflk2FcPX9RbqQrf6nqw61vgljbhuMflvgrZlSj-1YLgjCe_aUYiz7xISDQgN0MToL3i7CCuXylU_UpYgW94lKJC3kHXT6rzBwueddogTKrPpaSPP28RviizFcL594dEDUljbGjz3lpgZe5tBI-8jPtz9eGH-_oWU7kD_Upi6ZnVpuRdBmItjyFPS2stDPk4o8clPKgnBOpSMFlc2v5GkRYrZXJBRiDU4apmPUI4_Gn0qo1yBwKzp8jtOA6B3QEXoE4_WIJ3PSrdgD/jPad3pfPFhnb7Rup0uQmu4GjOahVRnYP/24)** --a sweeping, episode-by-episode journey through our nation's founding in honor of its 250th anniversary.

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this series invites you to learn about the principles, courage, sacrifice, and faith that made America possible--and _why this story still matters today_.

Filmed in the historic Indian Treaty Room in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in Washington, D.C., each episode brings a pivotal chapter of the American story to life.

**Here 's a glimpse of what you can access on your journey at no cost:****
**

* **The Declaration of Independence** -- _Larry P. Arnn, President, Hillsdale College_
How the Declaration of Independence defines who we are--and what it still asks of us

* **The Formation of the Army** -- _Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War_
The moment citizen-patriots took up arms and answered liberty's call against overwhelming odds

* **The King 's Call to Arms** -- _U.S. Senator Mike Lee_
When imperial authority collided with colonial defiance--and compromise was no longer possible

* **The Culper Spy Ring** -- _Brian Kilmeade, Co-Author, George Washington 's Secret Six_
The remarkable story of ordinary Americans who risked everything to outsmart the British and save the Revolution

* **Story of the American Soldier** -- _Michael Knowles, Author and Podcaster_
A tribute to the forgotten men whose sacrifice secured American independence

* **The U.S. Marine Corps Birthday** -- _Vice President J.D. Vance_
The enduring legacy of courage, service, and sacrifice that defines the U.S. Marine Corps

body:
65 days to go, and we are within striking distance.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/y1oVe9JEZR9?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810)
| |
# They said it would be a blowout. It isn't.
---
| | | | |
---
| |

Friend,
The _Albuquerque Journal_ [released its poll this morning](https://us.list-manage.com/4cZ4wnuF6nU?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810), and I want you to see the number before anyone tries to spin it for you.
**Deb Haaland 49. Gregg Hull 43.**
Six points, with 65 days until Election Day. The pollster who conducted it, Brian Sanderoff, said the margin was **narrower than a lot of people expected** , including him. The _Journal_ 's editorial board wrote that this is a horse race after all.
Think about what that number actually represents. My opponent came out of her primary with national name recognition, a former cabinet title, and a war chest many times the size of ours. Every bit of conventional wisdom said this race was over before Labor Day. Some people wrote us off in June.
We are six points back, and we got here without a single dollar of that Washington money. We got here because of you.
Here is why I am telling you this today instead of next week. **Eight percent of New Mexico voters have not made up their minds yet** , and starting this week my opponent will use her advantage to flood the airwaves from now until November 3. She will spend millions telling New Mexicans who I am before I get the chance to tell them myself.
I am not going to let that happen. But **I need to be on television, on the radio, and in mailboxes in every corner of this state** at the same time she is, and that takes resources we have to raise right now.
If you can contribute $25 today, that helps put our message in front of voters who have never heard my name. If you can do $50 or $100, that funds the door knocks and the phone calls in the counties that will decide this thing. And if you are able to give $250 or more, you are underwriting the TV time that keeps us on the air through Election Day.
---
| | | | | [YOU CAN CHIP IN HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/6P7NgLfRyvj?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810)
---
| |
Twelve years as Mayor of Rio Rancho taught me that you do not win by having the most money. You win by showing up, doing the work, and delivering results people can see in their own neighborhoods. That is how we grew Rio Rancho. That is how we doubled the police budget. That is how we kept Intel and brought in employers who are hiring New Mexicans right now.
And that is how we are going to win in November.
**Six points. Sixty-five days. Let's go.**
Thank you for standing with me,
---
|
---
| |
P.S. Nobody thought this race would be close. It is. Every dollar you give in the next 48 hours goes straight into reaching the voters who are still deciding. subject: I want to take a moment to talk about faith
body:
Taking a leap of faith.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In just a minute, I’m going to personally ask you to **[make a donation to my campaign for governor.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260830_2_leapoffaith.yH5b4x&refcode=em20260830-1956&amount=5&t=1&akid=1956%2E299639%2EwyhVJ6)**
Before I do, I hope you’ll let me share **an important lesson I’ve learned about faith.**
Back in 2021, the Texas GOP was ramming an extreme anti-voter bill through the State House. The voter suppression bill they were pushing was ugly. It was dangerous. And I knew that staying put would mean letting Texans lose their freedom to vote.
So I took a leap of faith. I walked off the floor.
But I knew I couldn’t stop this bill on my own. I needed my fellow Democratic legislators with me in order to break quorum. So I stood up, and I texted other legislators:
_“A leap of faith only works if you take it.”_
Together, we ran out the clock and stopped a bill designed to silence Texas voters. That quorum break protected Sunday morning voting — a sacred tradition in Black churches — and blocked a provision that would have allowed partisan judges to overturn election results without evidence. And we earned that victory together.
**Just like I needed my fellow Texas Democrats by my side on that day five years ago, I’m asking you to join me today.** I’m asking you to have faith that we can finally unseat corrupt Governor Greg Abbott and flip Texas together.
Each time you chip in to our people-powered campaign, you’re doing it alongside thousands of others who also believe in our power to win a brighter future for every Texan.
**[Can I count on you to donate to my grassroots campaign?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260830_2_leapoffaith.yH5b4x&refcode=em20260830-1956&amount=5&t=2&akid=1956%2E299639%2EwyhVJ6)**

_A leap of faith only works if you take it._ And when you do, others will leap with you.
— Gina

# [Proud to Fight to Strengthen Our Social Safety Nets!](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/08/30/proud-to-fight-to-strengthen-our-social-safety-nets/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on August 30, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 08.30.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=643da3d9a732bfb9fdb3fe4b21f9f5589f3a0b4a7e0a024aaf4fc77434d081da&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8815&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=884deb57cd5117921a44e5ac591d88ae&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=c588e5bf999f149ee122b29437439bf9)**
---
| **Adams Dem Picnic**
---
| |
---
Many thanks to the Adams County Democratic Committee for inviting me to speak at our annual picnic.
---
It was a terrific afternoon with other Americans who care deeply about our country. I was proud to announce my recent endorsements and to name my family and volunteers who also support this campaign. Fellow candidates Kathleen Pratt (PA-91st) and Todd Crawley (PA-193rd), as well as Todd Eagan from the Voter Protection Program, gave great speeches.
---
But of course, the pièce de résistance was the speech from PA State Representative Malcolm Kenyatta who is also Vice Chair of the DNC. He inspired us with important context about the marchers who walked across the Edmund Pettus Bridge in 1965 during the Civil Rights movement. Despite the odds stacked against them, they won their fight for civil rights and equality anyway because of their perseverance.
---
Boneyard BBQ served delicious food and volunteer Joyce Zeppa-Sadler kindly baked our pink lemonade and blueberry muffin tops for the candidate cookie contest.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=0deebdb55f289665fc0d218fa97d5979105895511243f88de8be138731b49d40&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8815&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=7646e2e88580738885689ecfbb861223&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=c588e5bf999f149ee122b29437439bf9) and patriotic fellowship!
---

---

Doorknocking in Adams County last Sunday!
---
Please vote for me, Beth Farnham, to represent us in the US House of Representatives!
---
Please reelect Josh Shapiro for Governor and Austin Davis for Lieutenant Governor!
---
Please elect Kathleen Pratt for Pennsylvania State House 91st District!
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=750b7f260355f491b34b88e9d25751a3c6b9a91b35dd1b5065aef904ceebeffb&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8815&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=b17d9e965f3f63ef3808bbe621d18376&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=c588e5bf999f149ee122b29437439bf9) !
---
| | **Our National Folly**
---
| |
---
“Let them race cars” is pretty much what Trump’s quote would be if he was Marie Antoinette.
---
Absolutely disgusting.
---
While Everyday Americans are struggling with the prices of gas in the tank, food on the table, healthcare, and housing, Trump is wasting millions of taxpayer dollars for security to race cars down the streets of Washington D.C.
---
Nevermind that Everyday Americans need those streets.
---
Nevermind that the business of the American people needs to continue.
---
Big Boy Trump wants fast cars.
---
And the John Joyces of Congress absolutely let him.
---
Vote him out by voting me in on November 3rd.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy!
---
Source: [https://www.forbes.com/sites/peterlyon/2026/08/24/trumps-grand-prix-race-was-fast-and-furious-but-was-it-tone-deaf/](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=64076a9fe275b082ff1916d5deac5b6834fd9b57096eb63568efaa8bf13ac0cb&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8815&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=10bf1bb49bd388417d9d2913ecce57e5&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZm9yYmVzLmNvbS9zaXRlcy9wZXRlcmx5b24vMjAyNi8wOC8yNC90cnVtcHMtZ3JhbmQtcHJpeC1yYWNlLXdhcy1mYXN0LWFuZC1mdXJpb3VzLWJ1dC13YXMtaXQtdG9uZS1kZWFmLw=&email_id=c588e5bf999f149ee122b29437439bf9)
---
| **Food Pantries Struggle More!**
---
| |
---
At the Central Penn Food Bank in Harrisburg in January.
---
Because hungry Pennsylvanians genuinely needed their SNAP benefits, but the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ended them, local food pantries try to serve more families.
---
Why?
---
Because Trump and his lackeys, like our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, don’t believe in feeding the hungry, helping the poor, healing the sick, or welcoming the stranger.
---
Oh sure, they’ll wave their Bibles around all day long, but we know them by their bitter fruits – starvation, malnutrition, disease transmission, and dead Americans at the hands of murderous masked agents of the state.
---
“Food banks and pantries say they expect demand for emergency food assistance to remain high as households adjust to changes in SNAP eligibility and rising food costs.”
---
Sidenote: SNAP benefits average $211 per person, per month.
---
Trump and the John Joyces of Congress are cruel people who only want to grift Everyday Americans out of their hard-earned dollars – see the ballroom, Grand Prix racing, and Trump coin, for example, and cut off services for those in need.
---
But it doesn’t have to be this way.
---
You can vote for me, Beth Farnham, to represent us from our 13th Congressional District, instead of John Joyce.
---
I’ll work with other caring members of Congress to strengthen our social safety nets like SNAP, Pennie, Medicare, and Medicaid so that no American ever goes hungry or without access to healthcare. And our local food pantries won’t be overwhelmed, but available to help those in a pinch.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and EACH OTHER!
---
| | |
At My Neighbor’s Bounty Food Pantry in June.
---|---|---
| **Bedford Dems Picnic**
---
| |
---
Many thanks to the Bedford County Democratic Committee for welcoming me to speak and eat at their potluck meeting on Tuesday.
---
It was great to connect with such a dedicated group of patriotic Americans who are energized to knock doors, make phone calls to voters, address postcards for my campaign, and more!
---
They were also a great comfort while we received the sad news that American legend and humanitarian Dolly Parton had passed away.
---
In other news, I participated in an informative farm tour in our absolutely stunning Congressional District. More to come!
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and our country!
---
Photo credit: Cindy Strait

| **Let’s Choose Each Other!**
---
| |
---
“...the deaths may even have been altogether fabricated by one of the Governor’s hopeful staffers,” Kennedy wrote on X.”
---
As if the death of an infant from measles wasn’t horrific enough, it’s utterly cruel and terrible that the U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services would ever imply that Governor Josh Shapiro would ever fabricate the scenario. RIP measles victims.
---
And where is our own U.S. Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, who wants everyone to know that he’s a retired dermatologist, in this awful turn of events?
---
Absolutely nowhere to be found.
---
He doesn’t care what RFK Jr. lies about. Any member of Trump’s administration is not to be questioned in his opinion, irresponsible rhetoric about the transmission of deadly disease be damned.
---
But you know I won’t hide from you.
---
In fact, I’ll have a Town Hall in Joyce’s backyard on October 4th at the AFSCME building.
---
Interested attendees MUST REGISTER.
---
You can scan the QR code in the graphic or click on this link: [https://forms.gle/EoLeVg53jFqaxA6DA](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=f11116515eb026cb1f8c3a4d513b354bd74a384bd03cb2fda2786a2c7304a396&blog_id=213069660&post_id=8815&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=267f0038e2a55aafaf01647645fcb1ab&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9mb3Jtcy5nbGUvRW9MZVZnNTNqRnFheEE2REE&email_id=c588e5bf999f149ee122b29437439bf9)
---
I’ll tell you about our stunningly beautiful 13th Congressional District and answer your questions on A.I. Data Centers, SNAP, and so much more.
---
Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and each other!
---
